problem_statement: LangChain's streaming support is inconsistent and unreliable across providers, features, and abstraction layers. Some provider/proxy configurations break streaming outright — for example, Anthropic served through Bedrock proxies omits the SSE 'event:' field, causing streaming calls to fail with 'No generation chunks were returned' rather than falling back gracefully or surfacing a clear error. Configuration options meant to control streaming behavior are themselves broken: setting disable_streaming='tool_calling' can crash with an AttributeError when a tool call forces a fallback to non-streaming, and separately causes streaming to be disabled for all turns whenever any tool is bound, not just tool-calling turns as documented. Structured-output streaming has its own defects independent of these: chunks emit spurious Pydantic serializer warnings because the typed 'parsed' field isn't excluded from serialization (a bug already fixed on the non-streaming code path but not ported to streaming), and response metadata such as HTTP headers (e.g., x-request-id) is silently dropped in structured-output streaming even though it is preserved in both non-structured streaming and non-streaming structured output, breaking observability and log correlation. At the agent-orchestration layer, the async agent factory calls ainvoke internally instead of astream, so on_llm_new_token callbacks never fire even when a user enables astream at the graph level — giving the false impression of real-time token streaming when none is occurring. Underlying all of this, the standard test suite and release process have gaps: tool_call_streaming profile data has known provider-specific inconsistencies (a Perplexity profile mismatch, MistralAI returning complete tool_call objects instead of tool_call_chunk deltas) that could cause premature enforcement of stricter streaming conformance tests, and existing test assertions for streaming error callback edge cases (empty generations) are already incorrect, indicating latent quality issues in how streaming error handling is verified.
target_user: Developers building applications on LangChain who rely on streaming responses from LLM providers — including those using Bedrock-proxied models, tool-calling agents, structured-output chains, and async agent/graph orchestration — and who need streaming to behave predictably and be observable in production.

user_stories.persona: a developer using Anthropic models via a Bedrock proxy
user_stories.action: get a clear error or automatic fallback when the proxy's SSE stream omits standard fields
user_stories.value: my application doesn't fail opaquely with 'no generation chunks were returned' and I can diagnose or recover from the incompatibility

user_stories.persona: a developer who sets disable_streaming='tool_calling' on a model with tools bound
user_stories.action: have streaming correctly disabled only for turns that actually trigger tool calls, without crashing
user_stories.value: I get the documented behavior instead of an AttributeError or unexpectedly non-streaming responses on every turn

user_stories.persona: a developer using structured output with streaming enabled
user_stories.action: receive chunks without spurious serializer warnings and with the same response metadata (like x-request-id) that non-streaming structured output provides
user_stories.value: my logs stay clean and I can correlate streamed responses with provider-side request logs

user_stories.persona: a developer building an async agent with graph-level astream enabled
user_stories.action: have the agent's underlying model calls actually stream tokens instead of silently using ainvoke
user_stories.value: my on_llm_new_token callbacks fire as expected and I can build genuine real-time UI experiences

user_stories.persona: a LangChain maintainer coordinating standard-test releases
user_stories.action: have accurate, provider-aware tool_call_streaming profile data and correct streaming error-callback test assertions before enforcing stricter conformance tests
user_stories.value: provider-specific quirks (like Perplexity or MistralAI) don't cause false test failures or premature breaking releases

acceptance_criteria.given: an Anthropic model is called through a Bedrock proxy that omits the SSE 'event:' field
acceptance_criteria.then: the client either successfully parses the stream via a fallback mechanism or raises a specific, actionable error identifying the missing SSE field, instead of a generic 'no generation chunks were returned' failure

acceptance_criteria.given: disable_streaming='tool_calling' is set and tools are bound to the model
acceptance_criteria.when: a turn does not trigger a tool call
acceptance_criteria.then: the response streams normally with no AttributeError and no fallback to non-streaming

acceptance_criteria.given: disable_streaming='tool_calling' is set and tools are bound to the model
acceptance_criteria.when: a turn triggers a tool call requiring fallback to non-streaming
acceptance_criteria.then: the fallback completes without raising AttributeError on the AsyncStream object

acceptance_criteria.given: structured output is requested with streaming enabled
acceptance_criteria.when: chunks are serialized (e.g., via model_dump or similar)
acceptance_criteria.then: no Pydantic serializer warning is emitted for the 'parsed' field

acceptance_criteria.given: structured output is requested with streaming enabled
acceptance_criteria.when: the provider returns response metadata such as HTTP headers (e.g., x-request-id)
acceptance_criteria.then: that metadata is present on the aggregated streamed response, matching what non-streaming structured output returns

acceptance_criteria.given: an async agent is invoked with graph-level astream enabled
acceptance_criteria.when: the agent calls the underlying chat model
acceptance_criteria.then: the model is invoked via astream (not ainvoke) and on_llm_new_token callbacks fire for each token produced

acceptance_criteria.given: the standard test suite's tool_call_streaming profile is run against Perplexity and MistralAI
acceptance_criteria.when: provider-specific behavior differs from the generic profile (e.g., complete tool_call instead of tool_call_chunk)
acceptance_criteria.then: the test suite reflects a documented per-provider exception rather than failing or forcing incorrect behavior

acceptance_criteria.given: the streaming error callback test for empty generations
acceptance_criteria.then: the assertion correctly matches the actual empty-generations shape with no false pass or false fail

success_metrics.target: 1 new regression test added and passing

out_of_scope: Building a universal SSE-compliance shim for arbitrary third-party proxies beyond the documented Bedrock case
Redesigning the overall streaming API or chunk data model
Adding new provider integrations or expanding tool_call_streaming to providers not currently covered by standard tests
General agent framework redesign beyond fixing the ainvoke/astream discrepancy
Performance optimization of streaming throughput or latency

risks.description: The finding is based on a small number of pain points (one issue each), so the true scope and downstream impact of each defect across the broader user base is not well established; prioritization is based on severity labels rather than confirmed frequency.
Fixing disable_streaming='tool_calling' touches fallback logic shared across many provider integrations, risking regressions in currently-working streaming paths.

Provider-specific quirks (Bedrock proxy SSE omission, MistralAI tool_call vs tool_call_chunk, Perplexity profile mismatch) may require ongoing per-provider maintenance rather than a one-time fix, since they stem from upstream API behavior LangChain does not control.
Tightening streaming standard tests before fixing known provider profile mismatches could break CI for integrations that are otherwise functioning, if sequencing is not carefully managed.
